title: He Shined Shoes for $5… and Gave Away $202,000
yt_title: He Shined Shoes for $5… and Gave Away $202,000 ❤️ #shorts
yt_description:
Every Tuesday and Thursday before sunrise, Albert Lexie pushed his purple shoeshine cart into Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh. A shine cost $5 and he earned about $10,000 a year – but every single tip went to the hospital's Free Care Fund for sick kids whose families couldn't pay.

Over 30+ years, he gave more than $202,000 – over a third of everything he ever earned. He called the patients "Albert's kids".

A true story. Sources: ABC News, NPR, UPMC Children's Hospital of Pittsburgh.

#unsungstories #truestory #kindness #inspiration #shorts
script: Every Tuesday and Thursday, before the sun came up, a man pushed a purple cart into a children's hospital in Pittsburgh. His name was Albert Lexie. He wasn't a doctor. He shined shoes. Five dollars a shine. He made about ten thousand dollars a year. But if you gave him six dollars... that extra dollar wasn't his. Every single tip went to the hospital's Free Care Fund, for sick kids whose families couldn't pay. One dollar. Then a hundred. Then a thousand. One Christmas, a doctor handed him a fifty-dollar bill. Straight to the kids. He kept doing it for more than thirty years. By the time he retired, in twenty thirteen, Albert had given over two hundred and two thousand dollars. More than a third of everything he ever earned. When people asked him why, his answer was simple. "I love my kids." The hospital called them patients. Albert called them... Albert's kids.
